editorial.headline: Non-Star Hotels: Nationally Open, Bali Depends on the Declared Scope
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 55106 covers commercially managed non-star accommodation for daily or weekly stays, but its Bali PMA position depends on how the exact activity resolves in OSS.
editorial.body:
KBLI 55106 is the commercial provision of non-star hotel accommodation, ordinarily offered on a daily or weekly basis. It applies where an operator manages all or part of a building that meets the requirements for a non-star hotel. The scope expressly accommodates both building-area bands: premises above 6,000 m² and premises at or below 6,000 m². The point is not a particular style of hospitality, but commercially managed short-stay accommodation within that non-star hotel framework.

The activity is open to small, medium and large businesses. That matters because the code does not reserve the field for a single operating scale: a modest accommodation business and a larger hotel operation can each sit within the stated scope, provided the actual activity fits it. Nationally, the PMA status is open, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign investment is not capped below full ownership at the national level for this activity.

Bali requires a more exact reading. The record does not mark the activity as categorically blocked for PMA registration in Bali; instead, it identifies the Bali outcome as scope-dependent. At the large scale, OSS risk may be low for some scopes and higher for others. PMA registration in Bali is available only by declaring the higher-risk scope, and the exact activity must be checked in live OSS. This is not a minor administrative footnote: it is the condition that determines whether the nationally open position can be used in Bali.

The reason is the province-wide, permanent Bali rule blocking all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities for PMA. For a founder, the honest conclusion is therefore precise rather than dramatic. KBLI 55106 is nationally open to PMA, including up to 100% foreign ownership, but Bali is neither an automatic yes nor a blanket no on this record. Its availability turns on the risk outcome of the exact declared scope in OSS, with PMA registration possible only where that declaration falls into the higher-risk path described in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: The true question in Bali is not whether the activity is nationally open, but what the exact declared scope resolves to in OSS.
